subject: Activation corridor validation / quiet-period decision for ACME private deployment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: CloudRamp Integrations <eng@cloudramp.io>, ACME Ops <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Activation corridor validation / quiet-period decision for ACME private deployment

Morning team —

Quick alignment before we flip traffic for ACME tonight. Summary of the activation corridor items I want explicit signoff on: 

- Network: BGP peering announced, MTU consistent at 9216 across fabric, ACLs and security groups applied, DNS TTLs lowered to 60s.
- Certificates: TLS certs loaded into customer HSM, OCSP stapling verified.
- Connectivity: VPN/Direct peer validated with 3 minute keepalive, syslog and metrics forwarding to ACME SIEM verified.
- Runtime: KV cache pre-warm policy executed, prefix cache primed for top-10 prefixes, warmup logs attached.
- Smoke: 5 synthetic traffic streams (100 reqs each) validating p95 < 120ms, 99th < 350ms, no 5xx, traces include trace-id propagation.
- Rollback/quiet window: 45 minute quiet window post-activation; automatic rollback if error rate > 0.8% for 10 minutes or sustained p95 > 300ms.

See attached activation-corridor-checklist.pdf. Please call out any blockers by 12:30 PDT so we have time to delay.

Desired outcome: greenlight or list of blockers + owners.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: eng@cloudramp.io <eng@cloudramp.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, ACME Ops <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation corridor validation / quiet-period decision for ACME private deployment

Jonas — thanks for the checklist. Quick notes from CloudRamp side after the final preflight: 

- BGP: routes are visible from both PoPs; we observed intermittent route flap at 02:13 UTC (attached sample), we throttled BGP flap-damping to 30s and the fabric stabilized. See net-trace-sample.pcap.
- MTU: one edge switch had MTU 1500 on a transit VLAN; we fixed this at 08:42 PDT.
- NTP: ACME's primary NTP server shows ~120ms jitter across a subset of hosts — we recommend enabling fallback pool.ntp.org for the activation window to avoid token expiry drift.
- Health checks: 3/4 healthprobe origins are passing; the remaining origin failed due to a firewall rule that missed the new redwood-prod-cidr. We opened a ticket and applied the rule at 08:58 PDT.

CloudRamp recommends a 60-minute quiet window instead of 45 given the NTP and recent flap history. We can shorten to 45 after 30 minutes of stable telemetry.

Attachment: net-trace-sample.pcap

—CloudRamp Eng
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, eng@cloudramp.io, ACME Ops <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation corridor validation / quiet-period decision for ACME private deployment

Thanks — going to call out two runtime points that require ops acknowledgement: 

1) KV Cache warmup: the attached kvcache-warmup-log.txt shows priming for the top-25 prefixes, but we only hit ~72% coverage vs the expected 85%. That leaves a cold tail for rarer prefixes which could spike p95 during the first 10 minutes. We should rate-limit traffic to 60% of usual to smooth the warmup.

2) Tracing/Logging: Make sure the trace sampling rate is bumped to 15% for the quiet window so we have better signal for root-cause. Also confirm that urgent traces are annotated with 'activation-corridor' tag — our observability pipelines rely on that for rapid dashboards.

If ACME Ops is comfortable with a staged ramp to 60% for first 12 minutes then 85% after 30 minutes, I can update the traffic steering policy.

-Karthik
From: ACME Ops <ops@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, eng@cloudramp.io
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation corridor validation / quiet-period decision for ACME private deployment

Jonas / team — acknowledged. We accept the staged ramp proposal and the 60 minute quiet window with the 30 minute reevaluation. Action items from ACME: 

- We enabled NTP fallback to pool.ntp.org and confirmed token TTL skew is <50ms now.
- Firewall rule for redwood-prod-cidr confirmed.
- SIEM syslog ingestion validated for both edge PoPs.

We will hold traffic at 60% for 12 minutes then evaluate telemetry for ramp. If anything goes into the alarm band (error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes), we will enact rollback and notify the group.

—ACME Ops (Sara Lee)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: ACME Ops <ops@acme.com>, eng@cloudramp.io
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation corridor validation / quiet-period decision for ACME private deployment — post-activation readout

Team — quick post-activation update and validation notes now that we closed the corridor: 

Summary (timeline):
- 2026-10-18 20:00 UTC: activation started with staged ramp (60% for 12m).
- 2026-10-18 20:18 UTC: traffic increased to 85% after stable telemetry.
- 2026-10-18 20:45 UTC: quiet window complete; no rollback triggered.

Telemetry highlights:
- Smoke tests: all 5 synthetic streams completed; p95 ranged 70–95ms; 99th 210–330ms depending on origin. 
- Errors: transient 500 spikes (0.14%) during first 4 minutes; traced to a single origin with a misapplied rate-limit; fixed via policy patch at 20:05 UTC.
- KV cache: warmup reached 88% coverage after 10 minutes (log attached). Cold tail impact negligible after warmup.

Outstanding items / follow-ups:
- Karthik: can you keep trace sampling at 15% for 72 hours and keep the activation-corridor tag?
- CloudRamp: please share the BGP flap mitigation notes for our runbook (we saw the 02:13 UTC event).
- ACME: confirm SIEM alert template for activation-corridor tag so we can onboard into post-deploy monitoring.

This looks like a successful activation; I'll file a short runbook addendum and share the link to the activation readout in the HS ticket.

Thanks everyone — nice work coordinating a quiet, controlled activation.

Jonas
